title.es: Modismos en una charla de amigos

es: Interpretar modismos en una conversación en audio y decidir si se usan en sentido literal o figurado, leyendo entre líneas lo que el hablante no dice abiertamente.

usesVocabulary: the ball is in your court
take it with a pinch of salt

vocabulary.en: the ball is in your court
take it with a pinch of salt

teaching.en: It was awkward at first, so Ana told a joke to break the ice, and within minutes everybody in the room was laughing.
teaching.es: Al principio fue incómodo, así que Ana contó un chiste para romper el hielo, y en pocos minutos todos en la sala se reían.
teaching.explanationEs: Figurado: romper el hielo es relajar un ambiente tenso; aquí no hay hielo de verdad.
segments: It was awkward at first, so Ana told a joke to break
the ice, and within minutes everybody in the room was laughing.
teaching.audioText: It was awkward at first, so Ana told a joke to break the ice, and within minutes everybody in the room was laughing.

teaching.en: The exam was a piece of cake: I finished in twenty minutes, although my friends thought that it was terribly difficult.
teaching.es: El examen fue pan comido: terminé en veinte minutos, aunque mis amigos pensaron que era terriblemente difícil.
teaching.explanationEs: A piece of cake = algo facilísimo; no hay ningún pastel. A veces quien lo dice exagera por modestia o por nervios.
segments: The exam was a piece of cake: I finished in twenty
minutes, although my friends thought that it was terribly difficult.
teaching.audioText: The exam was a piece of cake: I finished in twenty minutes, although my friends thought that it was terribly difficult.

teaching.en: We are all tired, so let's call it a day; tomorrow I will hit the books again before the exam.
teaching.es: Estamos todos cansados, así que dejémoslo por hoy; mañana volveré a ponerme a estudiar antes del examen.
teaching.explanationEs: Call it a day = parar de trabajar o estudiar por hoy; hit the books = estudiar con esfuerzo, sin golpes.
segments: We are all tired, so let's call it a day;
tomorrow I will hit the books again before the exam.
teaching.audioText: We are all tired, so let's call it a day; tomorrow I will hit the books again before the exam.

teaching.en: I gave you two options, so the ball is in your court now: it is your decision, and I will accept whatever you choose.
teaching.es: Te di dos opciones, así que ahora te toca decidir a ti: es tu decisión, y aceptaré lo que elijas.
teaching.explanationEs: Viene del tenis: la pelota está en tu campo, o sea, te toca mover ficha.
segments: I gave you two options, so the ball is in your court
now: it is your decision, and I will accept whatever you choose.
teaching.audioText: I gave you two options, so the ball is in your court now: it is your decision, and I will accept whatever you choose.

teaching.en: In winter the boys broke the ice on the pond with a long branch, and here the expression is literal, not figurative.
teaching.es: En invierno los chicos rompieron el hielo del estanque con una rama larga, y aquí la expresión es literal, no figurada.
teaching.explanationEs: Hay hielo de verdad: el contexto (winter, pond, branch) confirma el sentido literal frente al figurado.
segments: In winter the boys broke the ice on the pond with
a long branch, and here the expression is literal, not figurative.
teaching.audioText: In winter the boys broke the ice on the pond with a long branch, and here the expression is literal, not figurative.

teaching.en: If a tired colleague calls your plan interesting, take it with a pinch of salt and read between the lines, because she may be avoiding an awkward conversation.
teaching.es: Si una colega cansada dice que tu plan es interesante, tómalo con reservas y lee entre líneas, porque puede estar evitando una conversación incómoda.
teaching.explanationEs: Take it with a pinch of salt = no creerlo del todo; read between the lines = entender lo que no se dice abiertamente.
segments: If a tired colleague calls your plan interesting, take it with a pinch of
salt and read between the lines, because she may be avoiding an awkward conversation.
teaching.audioText: If a tired colleague calls your plan interesting, take it with a pinch of salt and read between the lines, because she may be avoiding an awkward conversation.

prompt.es: ¿Qué significa «break the ice» en este texto?

choices.text: To crack a frozen pond in the playground.
To relax a tense atmosphere.
To stop a fight between two classmates.

feedback.es: El contexto (alumnos tímidos, un juego, charlas al final de la hora) es social: el juego sirve para relajar el ambiente, no hay hielo real.

hint.es: ¿Hay hielo de verdad en el texto o solo estudiantes tímidos?

origin.text: The new students were shy, so the teacher played a game to break the ice. By the end of the first hour, they were chatting about football and music as if they had known each other for years.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige cómo fue el examen, según la hablante.

choices.text: It was impossible to finish on time.
It was cancelled at the last minute.
It was very easy for her.

feedback.es: A piece of cake = facilísimo; terminó antes que todos y revisó dos veces, así que no fue difícil ni se canceló.

hint.es: Fíjate en que terminó antes que los demás y todavía tuvo tiempo de revisar.

origin.audio: I thought the history exam was a piece of cake. I finished before everybody else, and while my classmates were still writing, I checked my answers twice. On my way out, the teacher smiled and asked me whether I had really read all the questions.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Se hace tarde, así que dejémoslo por hoy.»

answer.text: It is getting late, so let's call it a day

feedback.es: Call it a day se mantiene entero; so une el motivo (it is getting late) con la propuesta.

hint.es: Empieza por el motivo, It is getting late, y termina con el modismo.

prompt.es: ¿Literal o figurado? Elige cómo se usa «a piece of cake» aquí.

choices.text: Literal: Sara ate a real dessert.
Figurative: Sara found the day easy.
Figurative: Sara passed an exam easily.

feedback.es: Hay café y un postre real sobre la mesa: a piece of cake es literal y no significa «fácil»; el examen es de la hermana.

origin.text: After lunch, Sara sat in the garden and ate a piece of cake with her coffee. Her sister, who was studying for an exam, asked her whether the coffee shop on the corner was still open.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada modismo con su sentido figurado.

pairs: the ball is in your court

pairs.es: ahora te toca decidir a ti
entender lo que no se dice abiertamente

feedback.es: Los cuatro son figurados: estudiar con ganas, pasar la decisión, terminar la jornada y captar el mensaje implícito.

pairs: the ball is in your court

pairs.es: ahora te toca decidir a ti
entender lo que no se dice abiertamente

prompt.es: Escucha: ¿cómo se sentía la clase al empezar y qué cambió?

choices.text: The class was frozen by the cold weather in the room.
The class was nervous until the joke relaxed everybody.
The class was excited, but the joke made things worse.

feedback.es: Awkward y el silencio total indican incomodidad, y el chiste la disolvió: acabaron intercambiando teléfonos; el clima no tiene nada que ver.

origin.audio: The first lesson was awkward. Nobody knew anybody, and the room was completely silent. Then our teacher told a joke about his own terrible handwriting, and suddenly everybody relaxed. By the end of the hour we were swapping phone numbers.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla y elige qué deja entender «a piece of cake» por su tono.

choices.text: That she really found the interview easy and is proud.
That she is angry because the interview was too short.
That she hides her worry behind a confident comment.

feedback.es: La voz tensa y la confesión posterior de que llevaba días estudiando contradicen el «a piece of cake»: oculta su preocupación.

origin.audio: Two friends were chatting on the phone last night. One of them said that the interview was a piece of cake, but her voice sounded tense. The other asked whether she was nervous, and she admitted that she had been hitting the books for days. Then she said that the ball was in the director's court now, and that she was trying not to think about it. Finally, they agreed to call it a day and watch a film.

prompt.es: Escucha otra vez y elige cómo se usa «the ball is in the director's court».

choices.text: Figuratively: now the director has to make a decision.
Literally: the director is playing a game with a ball.
Figuratively: the director has already rejected her.

feedback.es: No hay pelota ni pista real: tras la entrevista le toca decidir a la directora, y por eso la hablante intenta no pensar en ello.

origin.audio: Two friends were chatting on the phone last night. One of them said that the interview was a piece of cake, but her voice sounded tense. The other asked whether she was nervous, and she admitted that she had been hitting the books for days. Then she said that the ball was in the director's court now, and that she was trying not to think about it. Finally, they agreed to call it a day and watch a film.

prompt.es: ¿Qué quiere realmente Mia de Tom en este correo?

choices.text: She wants Tom to reject both proposals politely.
She would like Tom to choose the second proposal.
She will decide by herself if Tom does not answer.

feedback.es: Dice «read between the lines: I would like the second one»: su preferencia está implícita, aunque se la deja decidir a él.

origin.text: Hi Tom, I sent you two proposals last week, so the ball is in your court. Take your time, and read between the lines: I would like the second one, but I do not want to pressure you, so please decide in the way that feels right.

prompt.es: Escribe: «Dejémoslo por hoy; el examen fue pan comido.»

answer.text: Let's call it a day; the exam was a piece of cake.
accepted: Let's call it a day; the exam was a piece of cake.
Let us call it a day. The exam was a piece of cake.
Let's call it a day. The exam was a piece of cake.
Let us call it a day; the exam was a piece of cake.
The exam was a piece of cake, so let's call it a day.
The exam was a piece of cake; let's call it a day.

feedback.es: Combina call it a day (parar por hoy) y a piece of cake (algo facilísimo) sin cambiar el orden de sus palabras.

origin.text: Dejémoslo por hoy; el examen fue pan comido.

prompt.es: ¿Cómo se usa «break the ice» en cada momento de este relato?

choices.text: Both times figuratively, to relax the group.
First figuratively, then literally.
First literally, then figuratively.

feedback.es: Junto al estanque hay hielo real y un palo; en la cena el silencio se rompe con una historia: literal primero y figurado después.

origin.text: We reached the lake in January. The pond was frozen, and the guide broke the ice with a long pole so the horses could drink. Later, at dinner, nobody spoke until the guide told a funny story that broke the ice for real.

prompt.es: Completa: «Al principio todos nos sentíamos algo incómodos.»

feedback.es: Awkward describe la incomodidad social que un modismo como break the ice ayuda a disolver.

origin.text: At the start of the workshop everybody felt a little ___, because nobody knew anybody and the silence lasted so long that one chair sounded loud.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué deja entender la hablante sobre la respuesta de su jefa.

choices.text: That the project is probably harder than her words suggest.
That the project is finished well ahead of schedule.
That the manager dislikes being asked questions.

feedback.es: Las miradas al reloj y el final anticipado contradicen «a piece of cake»: la hablante lee entre líneas que el proyecto es más difícil.

origin.audio: I asked my manager whether the project was going well. She smiled and said that it was a piece of cake, but she kept looking at her watch, and then she suggested that we call it a day an hour early. I do not think she really meant it.
